fact: The Rwanda Standards Board (RSB) signed mutual recognition arrangements with Congo's ACONOQ and the Standards Association of Zimbabwe in Kigali on 6 March 2026, acting as Rwanda's national standards body.

The Zambia Bureau of Standards and the Rwanda Standards Board signed a technical cooperation agreement on standardisation and conformity assessment at the 32nd ARSO General Assembly in Mombasa, the document treating RSB as a national standards body.

KOICA committed a US$8 million grant for 2024-2028 to the Rwanda Standards Board to advance industrial standardisation with ICT tools, launched on 28 June 2024; the document names no IT or data standard.

ISO states that the Rwanda Standards Board is a government institution created in 2002 that has developed and published more than 4,130 standards, covering food, engineering, service, water, chemistry and consumer products, with no IT or data standard named; the statement is in a document published 9 October 2025.

The Official Gazette special issue of 20 November 2025 carries a notice in which the Rwanda Standards Board (RSB), established under Law N° 50/2013, publishes a list of standards as National Standards; the passages read do not show the list or name any information technology or data standard.

Law N° 50/2013 of 28 June 2013 establishes the Rwanda Standards Board (RSB) with legal personality and autonomy, and gives it the mission to establish and publish national standards, defined as RSB-approved standards whose compliance is not mandatory; it names no information technology or data standard.
